name: 6-Phosphogluconate Dehydrogenase Deficiency

criteria.description: Reduced or absent 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase enzyme activity in red blood cells
Presence of chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia
Identification of pathogenic variants in the 6PGD gene via molecular genetic testing
Exclusion of other red blood cell enzyme deficiencies such as G6PD deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Reduced 6PGD enzyme activity plus either genetic confirmation or clinical evidence of chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires differentiation from other hemolytic anemias and enzyme deficiencies.

searchTerms: chronic anemia from red blood cell breakdown
yellow skin from red blood cell breakdown
skin pallor due to low blood counts
fatigue related to low red blood cells
gallstones caused by chronic red cell breakdown
small areas of spleen tissue death

rare.symptomName: Severe hemolytic crisis triggered by infections or oxidative stress
searchTerms: red blood cell breakdown triggered by illness
hemolytic crisis from stress or infection

rare.symptomName: Growth retardation due to chronic anemia
searchTerms: growth delay from low red blood cells
poor growth caused by chronic anemia

laboratory: Decreased 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase enzyme activity in erythrocytes
Elevated indirect bilirubin and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)
Peripheral blood smear showing anisocytosis and polychromasia without spherocytes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in the 6PGD gene identified by sequencing
other: Exclusion of G6PD deficiency and other red cell enzyme defects by enzyme assays

distinguishingFeatures: G6PD deficiency typically presents with episodic hemolysis triggered by oxidative stress
G6PD enzyme assay differentiates from 6PGD deficiency
Different genetic mutations and inheritance patterns
Pyruvate kinase deficiency causes chronic hemolytic anemia with different enzyme defect
Often more severe anemia and reticulocytosis

redFlags: Severe hemolytic crisis with rapid anemia worsening
Neonatal jaundice requiring phototherapy or exchange transfusion
Splenic enlargement causing abdominal pain or hypersplenism
